title: Grateful Dead Live at Hill Auditorium on 1971-12-15
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> Samplitude Professional v10.2 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: A crisp soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1971 show highlighted by a smoking Dark Star, soaring Keith piano and tight band interplay.
ai_review.review: The Charlie Miller transfer delivers an exceptionally clear soundboard recording that showcases the Dead at peak form in late ’71.  The performance is charged with high energy – Dark Star, Lovelight, China>Rider and Mr. Charlie are repeatedly called “smoking,” while Keith’s piano is front‑and‑center and Pigpen is in top form.  Minor mix quirks (Keith a touch loud, Phil low) do not detract from the overall brilliance.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive 5‑star reviews praise both the musical performance and the clear soundboard source; only a few minor mix complaints keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear and well‑balanced overall. Keith’s piano is unusually prominent (some find it too loud), Phil’s bass is a bit recessed, occasional left‑channel buzz, but the mix remains highly listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Seamless transitions and tight set structure; the band moves fluidly from high‑octane rock to exploratory jams.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for soaring tone, solid guitar work and “sky‑high” playing throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Often noted as too low in the mix; bass presence is weaker than ideal.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals described as terrific and well‑controlled; his voice shines on his songs.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano is a highlight – on fire, prominent solos (You Win Again, Run Rudolph Run) and energetic comping; some feel it overwhelms the mix.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s kick sometimes buried while cymbals are bright; overall drumming tight and supportive.
